17C.11 It is vanity to desire riches.

precepts.text: Men of low degree are vanity and men of high degree are a lie; laid in the balance they are altogether lighter than vanity, so the life we have is vain and short-lived.
precepts.point: When you die you take no wisdom and no riches with you. A man heaps up riches and does not even know who shall gather them.

note.label: Psalm 39: David Mourns His Frailty and Prays to Recover Strength

precepts.why:
“verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity.” Psalm 62 says it of every rank of man: “Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity.” So the life we have is vain and short-lived. At your prime you are nothing; you cannot measure up to the Most High.

David asks the Lord to make him know his end and the measure of his days, that he may know how frail he is; this is him going through his affliction and thinking on his own death. Men's lives are short, and the sentence for all flesh is death. When you die you take no wisdom and no riches with you: a man “heapeth up riches, and knoweth not who shall gather them.”

Look at how the Most High cut down our days, from the hundreds of years he originally gave to 120, then to 70. You rarely see people pass 100 years. “thou hast made my days as an handbreadth; and mine age is as nothing before thee”.

precepts.text: Drought and heat consume the snow waters; so does the grave those which have sinned. The grave is what waits for those who commit sin, and that is what David is referring to.
precepts.point: When the Most High rebukes a man for iniquity, he makes his beauty consume away like a moth. When man commits iniquity the Lord corrects, and many times people end up dying when they commit iniquity.

note.label: Psalm 39: David Mourns His Frailty and Prays to Recover Strength

precepts.why:
“When thou with rebukes dost correct man for iniquity, thou makest his beauty to consume away like a moth”. Job shows what that consuming is: “Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned.” The grave is what waits for those who commit sin, and that is what David is referring to. When man commits iniquity the Lord corrects, and many times people end up dying when they commit iniquity.

This is what we must keep in mind as we walk: there is really one thing waiting for us if we are not keeping the commandments, and that is the grave. For some who keep the commandments the grave may still come, but eternal life waits after it. David understood this, which is why he repented.

precepts.text: When our mind goes astray and we end up in sin, we return and seek him ten times more; committing iniquity does not mean you cannot recover strength.
precepts.point: Everybody who comes into the truth is going to mess up and commit transgression, and everybody ends up where David ended up, having to ask forgiveness and be pardoned. The Lord continually afflicted David for his iniquity, and a lot of us are being afflicted for our iniquities to this very day, so we must come to the Lord with this mindset.

note.label: Psalm 39: David Mourns His Frailty and Prays to Recover Strength

precepts.why:
“O spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go hence, and be no more.” Spare me that I may recover strength means forgive my sins so I may bounce back before I die. Baruch shows how the bouncing back is done: “For as it was your mind to go astray from God: so, being returned, seek him ten times more.” When our mind goes astray and we end up in sin, we return and seek him ten times more. Committing iniquity does not mean you cannot recover strength.

That should be our thought too. Nobody knows when they will die; you could die tomorrow or in two seconds from a bullet, so your main focus must be to recover your strength before you go to the grave.

Everybody who comes into the truth is going to mess up and commit transgression, and everybody ends up where David ended up, having to ask forgiveness and be pardoned. The Lord continually afflicted David for his iniquity, and a lot of us are being afflicted for our iniquities to this very day, so we must come to the Lord with this mindset: “Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear unto my cry; hold not thy peace at my tears”.

points: David says he will keep his mouth with a bridle. A bridle is the bit you see in a horse's mouth that you use to move it whichever way you want; it is a restraint. So he restrains his mouth when the wicked is before him.
